items.title: Clarence "Little Dad" Vincent Interview, 1960-01-21
items.q: This is with Walter Burke. And you know the Hill City Bears.

ctx.x: Ask him what his name is.

What is his real name? What is his real name? Abraham Burdenhill. Abraham Burdenhill. Abraham Burdenhill. You know where it is? Burdenhill. This is with Walter Burke. And you know the Hill City Bears.
Ask him was a Hill City Band a brass band or a dance band or both?

items.title: Clarence "Little Dad" Vincent Interview, 1959-12-11
items.q: Walter Burke, he was a good musician of the truth. ... He was with the Head City Band.

ctx.x: Ask him if he knew, uh...

Now, this fella, Charlie V. Lyle, he's from Baton Rouge. He was a magician of the truth. He could play any kind of instrument. He just liked, he liked, he liked, composed, anything. Uh, Walter Burke, he was a good musician of the truth. Where was he from? He had a daughter, you know. Where was he from, Walter Burke? About his age. Uh, he was with the Head City Band. That man, Charlie Vidal, you know. And, uh, he was a good piano player. I mean, a good soundball player, a musician, a water voice. And he learned…
He survived and talked to everybody.

items.title: Clarence "Little Dad" Vincent Interview, 1959-11-17
items.q: And Walter Burke and that band and Charlie Vidal... And there was Walter Birch, he used to play with the Hill City too over there

ctx.x: Hill City, say. Yeah, that's old. I went to bed around about three or four years old. And my brother used to play it. My oldest brother. And Walter Burke and that band and Charlie Vidal. You ever heard of Charlie Vidal? Now what did he play? He's a little fella like me. What did he play? He played chord it, clarinet, violin, bass, guitar, any kind of. All around me. Yeah, he was really a professor. And he could play too. And at first I thought he just could play his violin. So I went up there, I was playing…
And get the instruments. What instruments?
